fit: Tamr Ajwa preparations in laboratory fermentation and cell assays
assessment: The experiment used human donor faecal cultures and an intestinal cell line. No participant received a treatment for pain. Preserve the later 2015 human dietary study as a separate design.

fit: wild date-palm extract and animal nociception
assessment: The highest tested extract arm had a longer hot-plate response at 120 minutes. The preparation, species and acute mouse endpoint differ. Separate reduced activity can complicate interpretation of response latency.

fit: Ajwa pulp fraction and chemical liver injury
assessment: This is a mouse liver outcome rather than clinical pain. Groups differ in the printed model-agent schedule, and the exposure was extracted pulp.

fit: Ajwa fruit-pulp extract and experimental lung injury
assessment: Lung histology and tissue markers concern induced injury. The article does not measure chronic pain severity following consumption of whole dried fruit.

fit: pitted Deglet Noor active comparator in an older-adult protocol
assessment: The preprint confirms the date cultivar and recruitment for NCT05358210. No comparator estimate or dedicated Parkinson pain scale is reported.

fit: pitted Deglet Noor and planned cognition measures
assessment: This is the protocol and recruitment report for NCT05358210. It gives no results and no separate apathy outcome.

fit: different date-palm species and mouse activity measures
assessment: The wild date-palm pulp extract produced behavioural and sedative measures in mice. These outcomes do not address clinical apathy or consumption of dried Phoenix dactylifera fruit.
